sections.h2: Where is the Rhea County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Rhea County Register of Deeds is at 375 Church Street, Suite 106, Dayton, TN 37321, and the phone is 423-775-7841.

Tennessee records land at the county level, so a deed for any Rhea County house, whether in Dayton, Graysville, Spring City or a rural stretch of the county, goes to this one office. Call before you drive over. Ask for the current recording fee schedule, the hours for the day you plan to visit and whether the office wants the original signed deed or accepts another format.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Rhea County?
sections.html:
The register sets a per-page recording fee, and you should get that figure by phone at 423-775-7841. The tax portion is fixed by the state and is the larger part of the bill on most sales.

State recordation chargeRateExample in Rhea County
Realty transfer tax on a deed$0.37 per $100$762.20 on a $206,000 sale
Mortgage (indebtedness) tax on a deed of trust$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exempt$204.70 on a $180,000 loan

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue, recordation tax rates. The $206,000 figure is the Census median owner-occupied value for Rhea County, used here only as a round example. The page fee for the register's own work is added to each total.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Rhea County home sale?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100. The Department of Revenue's help desk says it applies to all transfers of realty and is generally based on the greater of the price paid or the property's value, and it cites Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

Because the rule uses the greater of price or value, a deed that states a very low price for a house worth more does not lower the tax. Sellers who plan a family sale or a sale below market should talk to the title agent about the figure before the deed is signed. A buyer's lender adds a second charge, the indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 of the loan after the first $2,000, when the deed of trust is recorded.

Your sale contract decides which side pays each line, so read the settlement statement before closing day. If the register's total at the counter does not match the title company's estimate, ask the staff to walk through it.

sections.h2: Which Rhea County offices handle the rest of a sale?
sections.html:
The deed is one stop. The county's department list puts the other two property offices in the same building at 375 Church Street in Dayton.

  • Rhea County Property Assessor, Suite 100, 423-775-7840: parcel values and ownership maps
  • Rhea County Trustee, Suite 110, 423-775-7810: property tax bills and payoff amounts
  • Rhea County Register of Deeds, Suite 106, 423-775-7841: recording of the deed and mortgage

Order matters at closing. Get a tax payoff from the Trustee, send it to the title company, and have the register record the deed afterward. Ask the Trustee which year's bill is open and whether interest or delinquent amounts are attached, since back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: What should you ask the register before you close in Rhea County?
sections.html:
A short list of questions saves a second trip. Put them to the staff at 423-775-7841.

  • What is the total recording fee for a deed of my page count?
  • Does the deed need any reference to a prior book and page?
  • Has the office received the release for the mortgage being paid off?
  • How will the recorded original be returned, and how long does it take?
  • Can a title company record by an electronic method, or does it need to deliver the paper?

The register's answers apply on the day you ask, and fees and forms can change. If you sell as-is to a buyer who pays cash, the deed is usually the only document at the register, so the visit is quick when the paperwork is ready.

sections.h2: How is Rhea County laid out for a seller?
sections.html:
Rhea County covers 336 square miles, of which 21 are water, and its 315 square miles of land held about 104 people per square mile in 2020. Walden Ridge on the Cumberland Plateau forms the western edge. The Tennessee River marks the border with Meigs County in the east, and Whites Creek separates Rhea from Roane County to the north.

Watts Bar Dam crosses the Tennessee River near Spring City. The lake above the dam is Watts Bar Lake, and the lake below it is Chickamauga Lake. The Watts Bar Nuclear Generating Station stands near the dam. U.S. Route 27 is the main north-south road. State Route 30 meets it in Dayton, and State Route 68 links Spring City with Madisonville and Crossville.

Dayton is the county seat and largest town, with Graysville and Spring City as the two towns. The county sits in the Eastern Time Zone, and Bledsoe and Cumberland counties to the west keep Central Time. The Dayton micropolitan area belongs to the Chattanooga-Cleveland-Dalton combined statistical area.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Rhea County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 34,844 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.8 percent from the April 2020 base. It lists 15,955 housing units and 13,475 households. Owners live in 71.5 percent of occupied homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $206,000 for 2020 to 2024.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,326, and owners without one report $365. Median gross rent is $839. Median household income is $55,033, and 14.0 percent of residents are below the poverty line. Workers face a mean commute of 29.5 minutes, the longest of the four Tennessee counties compared in that table. The county issued 151 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What history shapes Rhea County today?
sections.html:
Rhea County was founded in 1807 and named for John Rhea, a Tennessee politician and Revolutionary War veteran. A portion of the Trail of Tears crossed the county in the 1830s. The county seat moved from the Washington community to Dayton in 1890 after the Cincinnati-Chattanooga Railroad reached Smith's Crossroads and Chattanooga grew.

The Scopes Trial took place at the Rhea County Courthouse in 1925, and William Jennings Bryan died in Dayton soon after it ended. Statues of Bryan and of defense lawyer Clarence Darrow stand on the courthouse grounds. Bryan College, named for William Jennings Bryan, is in Dayton, Chattanooga State Community College has a small campus there, and Rhea County Schools sends high school students to Rhea County High School in Evensville. Dayton City School serves grades K through 8 inside the city.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Rhea County?
faqs.a: At the Rhea County Register of Deeds, 375 Church Street, Suite 106, Dayton, TN 37321. The phone number is 423-775-7841.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Rhea County sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100, generally on the greater of the price paid or the property's value. On a $206,000 sale that comes to $762.20, before the register's own recording fee.

faqs.q: Is there a mortgage tax in Rhea County?
faqs.a: Yes. Tennessee charges $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness when a deed of trust is recorded, and the first $2,000 is exempt. A $180,000 loan owes $204.70.

faqs.q: Who gets my property tax payoff in Rhea County?
faqs.a: The Rhea County Trustee, 375 Church Street, Suite 110, at 423-775-7810. Ask for the open balance and any interest to your closing date, and give it to the title company.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rhea County house if the deed is still in a parent's name?
faqs.a: A title agent has to resolve who holds title before a buyer can close. Ask the register at 423-775-7841 what the recorded chain of deeds shows, and bring the findings to an attorney or title company.
